title: Advanced mass spectrometry technique breaks free from specialist hardware
excerpt: Researchers at the University of Warwick and spinout company Verdel Instruments have successfully demonstrated two-dimensional mass spectrometry (2DMS) on a benchtop instrument, making this powerful technique practical and affordable for everyday laboratory use.
content_html:
Researchers at the University of Warwick and spinout company Verdel Instruments have successfully demonstrated two-dimensional mass spectrometry (2DMS) on a benchtop instrument, making this powerful technique practical and affordable for everyday laboratory use.

Modern mass spectrometry workflows are built to reduce complexity before measurement: Chromatography separates, acquisition methods filter and processing pipelines simplify. These steps are essential, but they come at a cost—information is lost, often without the analyst knowing what's missing.

"The field has long recognized the power of 2DMS, but it has simply not been accessible—only the best-funded centers could afford the specialist hardware," said Tim Wilson, CEO of Verdel Instruments. "Our technology makes 2DMS possible on benchtop instruments, which are widely available. Any lab can now access this powerful technique."

In their paper, published in Analytical Chemistry, the Verdel/Warwick team provides the first demonstration of 2DMS on a commercially available quadrupole time-of-flight (Q-TOF) instrument, using an upgrade kit. They call this Q-2DMS, and the paper shows how it can be used to obtain high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry data from complex mixtures without the need for chromatographic separation or mass filtering.

The Q-2DMS method works by giving each analyte a unique frequency signature based on its mass-to-charge ratio. When these break apart during analysis, the fragments formed retain this signature, allowing a mathematical decoding process to instantly reveal which fragments came from which analytes.

What would normally be an unusable mess of signals becomes an ordered series of mass spectra similar to those obtained using conventional separation and filtering techniques, but now including information that is often lost.

The recently published paper shows that Q-2DMS preserved up to tenfold more usable spectral information when analyzing closely related or near-isobaric compounds.

The technique demonstrated in the paper could support work across several research areas, including:

  • Health care, for faster identification of unexpected drug metabolites, enabling more personalized treatment.
  • Environmental safety, as any laboratory can now directly detect emerging contaminants (PFAS) without pre-separation, accelerating water safety monitoring.
  • Drug control, for rapid characterization of novel synthetic drugs and designer compounds.
  • Drug development, for discovery of unanticipated reaction products and impurities.

Dr. Shum Prakash, business development manager at Warwick Innovations, said, "Years of world-leading research have led to Warwick spinout Verdel Instruments launching Q-2DMS. It combines high-resolution, easy-to-use readouts with a complete timestamp of each sample, so researchers can revisit the data later without needing the original sample, which may have degraded."

"What excites us most is what we don't yet know," concludes Peter O'Connor, professor of chemistry at the University of Warwick and senior author of the paper. "By making this technique accessible, we're enabling scientists worldwide to ask questions they couldn't ask before, and to find answers they weren't necessarily looking for."

content_html_zh:
华威大学和衍生公司 Verdel Instruments 的研究人员在台式仪器上成功演示了二维质谱 (2DMS)，使这种强大的技术实用且适合日常实验室使用。

现代质谱工作流程旨在降低测量前的复杂性：色谱分离、采集方法过滤和处理管道简化。 这些步骤是必要的，但它们是有代价的——信息丢失，而且分析师通常不知道丢失了什么。

Verdel Instruments 首席执行官 Tim Wilson 表示：“该领域早已认识到 2DMS 的强大功能，但它一直无法获得——只有资金最充足的中心才能负担得起专业硬件。” “我们的技术使 2DMS 在广泛使用的台式仪器上成为可能。 现在任何实验室都可以使用这项强大的技术。”

Verdel/Warwick 团队在《分析化学》上发表的论文中，使用升级套件在市售四极杆飞行时间 (Q-TOF) 仪器上首次演示了 2DMS。 他们称之为 Q-2DMS，论文展示了如何使用它从复杂混合物中获取高分辨率串联质谱数据，而无需色谱分离或质量过滤。

Q-2DMS 方法的工作原理是根据每种分析物的质荷比赋予其独特的频率特征。 当这些在分析过程中分解时，形成的片段保留了这种特征，从而允许数学解码过程立即揭示哪些片段来自哪些分析物。

通常无法使用的混乱信号变成了一系列有序的质谱，类似于使用传统分离和过滤技术获得的质谱，但现在包括经常丢失的信息。

最近发表的论文表明，在分析密切相关或接近同量异位的化合物时，Q-2DMS 保留了多达十倍的可用光谱信息。

论文中演示的技术可以支持多个研究领域的工作，包括：

  • 医疗保健，更快地识别意外的药物代谢物，从而实现更个性化的治疗。
  • 环境安全，因为任何实验室现在都可以直接检测新兴污染物 (PFAS)，无需预先分离，从而加速水安全监测。
  • 药物控制，用于快速表征新型合成药物和设计化合物。
  • 药物开发，用于发现意外的反应产物和杂质。

Warwick Innovations 业务开发经理 Shum Prakash 博士表示：“多年的世界领先研究促使 Warwick 分拆公司 Verdel Instruments 推出了 Q-2DMS。 它将高分辨率、易于使用的读数与每个样本的完整时间戳相结合，因此研究人员可以稍后重新访问数据，而无需使用可能已退化的原始样本。”

“最让我们兴奋的是我们还不知道的事情，”华威大学化学教授、该论文的资深作者彼得·奥康纳总结道。 “通过使这项技术变得可用，我们使世界各地的科学家能够提出他们以前无法提出的问题，并找到他们不一定要寻找的答案。”
